messages:
sasha: Heads up — seeing a spike in GPU pods Pending in eu-west1a, started ~15m ago. lots of tiny gang jobs stuck, eviction churn rising.

maya: seeing that too. prometheus shows pending_gpu_count up x3 since 10:12. any obvious taint/affinity failures in scheduler logs?

jon: pulled kube-scheduler logs for the window. repeated predicate failures: "node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity" and "Insufficient resource: nvidia.com/gpu" but nodes report free GPUs. also a few "failed to attach network: conntrack limit exceeded" warnings from CNI.

sasha: pasted excerpt from scheduler: ```I0322 10:14:05.123456 1 scheduler.go:456] Pod test-gang-7 failed predicate MatchNodeSelector: node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity; failing nodes: [g-eu-a-03 g-eu-a-02]```

sasha: and CNI logs: ```W0322 10:13:58.999999 1 conntrack.go:89] conntrack: syscall nfnetlink_recv_recv failed: no space left on device```

lee: conntrack exhaustion could make kube-proxy/CNI drop flows and lead to transient label sync failures. are we seeing attach/detach flapping on those nodes?

jon: yes. attach-detach controller shows a backlog: several volumes and network interfaces queued for attach for >60s. warm-pool node shows repeated `Attach` -> `Detach` -> `Attach` in a 2m window.

maya: could be correlated: nodes hit conntrack limit -> kubelet/CNI fail to apply pod networking -> our mutation webhook times out -> pod admission marks node unschedulable for affinity checks?

sasha: hypothesis: tight nodeAffinity + topologySpread + gang scheduling together make scheduler reject nodes that are temporarily mis-labeled or network-unready. fleet then tries to preempt lower-priority pods, which churns GPUs and wastes compute.

lee: quick mitigation options: 1) relax affinity for small-gang test queues (non-prod) to avoid gang lock, 2) bump conntrack on affected nodes (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max), 3) add a small grace window in scheduler predicate for network-ready label.

jon: I ran `kubectl describe node g-eu-a-02` — Node Ready True but CNI plugin reports "NetworkUnavailable: true" briefly. Here's relevant snippet: ```Conditions: Ready=True MemoryPressure=False NetworkUnavailable=True```

maya: ops/infra, can we bump conntrack on eu-west1a hosts safely? what's current value?

infra-bot: deploy plan exists: conntrack bump to 524288 on pool eu-west1a nodes. will roll via daemonset with cordon+drain disabled. schedule window 20m.

lee: if we do that, we should also tweak our scheduler's pod topology predicate fallback: allow placement if node has transient NetworkUnavailable condition cleared within last 30s. might be safer than relaxing affinity globally.

sasha: agreed — make smaller change to scheduler plugin first for canary, target non-prod queue. idea: add node-liveness grace when node condition flips quickly.

jon: i'll open a tiny PR against our custom predicate with a flag `--node-grace-seconds=30` default 0. will test in staging.

maya: ops, start conntrack bump in eu-west1a canary (2 nodes) and monitor pending_gpu_count + attach-detach queue. set alert if pending doesn't drop in 10m.

infra-bot: canary started on nodes g-eu-a-08,g-eu-a-09. daemonset applied with sysctl kernel parameter.

sasha: after canary: pending_gpu_count down 60% on those racks, attach queue cleared. but other AZs still spike; might be cascading because scheduler moves pods cross-az.

lee: long-term we should: 1) ensure conntrack headroom on GPU nodes (our workloads open many ephemeral connections), 2) add a scheduler fallback to prefer nodes with stable network condition history, 3) re-evaluate affinity rules on small parallel batch jobs (they can tolerate spread).

jon: noted for postmortem: eviction churn increased cost ~2 GPU-hours in last hour in eu-west1a. capture runbooks: if conntrack errors appear, run `ss -s` && `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count` and escalate to infra.

maya: adding runbook snippet: ```# check conntrack usage
ssh node
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
# bump temporarily
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
# persist via /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf
```

sasha: thanks everyone. jon please post PR link when ready; lee can we get a quick quant on how many small-gang jobs use strict affinity? might help scope scheduler change.

lee: will query bigquery for `pod_label:small-gang` + nodeAffinity usage and report back in #eng-platform in 30m.

sasha: follow-ups: - roll scheduler grace flag to staging today - conntrack bump network canary in eu-west1a - monitor cost/eviction metrics and reopen if not improved. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: canary completed: no regressions observed. will schedule wider roll in 1h unless blocked.
